userStories.title: Keep replied GitLab nax notes top-level and fail closed on unknown PR lists
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Restore durable top-level nax notes after GitLab replies and prevent duplicate PR creation when the PR list is unreadable.

**Motivation** — On GitLab a human's reply under nax's summary is also invisible to the review, because `triage` drops threads opened by nax.

**Approach** — **C1: flatten replied nax top-level notes on GitLab.** GitHub has no replies to top-level comments: a response is a new top-level comment. GitLab's reply converts the note into a discussion. The GitLab readers restore GitHub's shape: a discussion with `individual_note === false` whose first non-system note has no `position` and carries a nax-bot marker whose key is one of `TOP_LEVEL_MARKER_KEYS` (`summary`, `w-index`, `w-evidence`, `fix-summary`) is returned by `listPrComments` as top-level comments (every non-system note, in order, `kind: "comment"`) and is left out of `listReviewThreads`. Every consumer then works unchanged: own-comment lookups find the note, and a human's reply reaches the review as a top-level comment behind the existing writer gate. The marker alone does not establish ownership: flattening changes only how a discussion is classified, and `ownComments` still requires the authenticated login. Item threads (`w-<id>.<hash>`) and finding threads (`f-…`) are never flattened.

`src/forge/marker.ts` imports `listPrComments` from `src/forge/threads.ts`, so `threads.ts` cannot import the marker parser from `marker.ts` without a runtime cycle (`check:import-cycles`). The marker grammar moves to a new leaf, `src/forge/marker-grammar.ts`; `marker.ts` imports from it and re-exports `isNaxBotMarkerKey` and `parseNaxBotMarker`, so `@/forge` exports are unchanged.

`hasOpenPr` throws on unparseable or non-array output; its three callers (`auto-pr` `shouldRun` and `execute`, `openDraftFinishPr`) already treat a throw as "unknown, do not open".

**Scope** — In: marker grammar extraction, public forge exports, GitLab reader classification, PR-list parse errors, and GitLab publish-index reuse. Out: finding unresolve writes (US-002), item reopening (US-003–US-005), settlement display (US-006–US-007), and ready/push changes (US-008). A GitLab discussion opened by someone else with a forged top-level marker is flattened into top-level comments; it gains no ownership and stays behind the writer gate.

**Interface** — Marker grammar. Baseline: `MARKER_KEY_PATTERN`, `markerPattern`, `isNaxBotMarkerKey`, `parseNaxBotMarker` in `src/forge/marker.ts`. Target: in new `src/forge/marker-grammar.ts`, plus `export const TOP_LEVEL_MARKER_KEYS = ["summary", "w-index", "w-evidence", "fix-summary"] as const`; `marker.ts` imports and re-exports `isNaxBotMarkerKey` and `parseNaxBotMarker`; `src/forge/index.ts` also exports `TOP_LEVEL_MARKER_KEYS`.

`listPrComments(ref, deps, cwd)`. Baseline: GitLab keeps `individual_note === true` discussions only. Target: also returns every non-system note of a flattened discussion (Approach, C1), as `kind: "comment"`, in discussion order.

`listReviewThreads(ref, deps, cwd)`. Baseline: GitLab keeps every `individual_note === false` discussion. Target: leaves flattened discussions out.

`hasOpenPr(forge, branch, deps, cwd)`. Baseline: unparseable or non-array JSON returns `false`. Target: throws `NaxError` `FORGE_PR_LIST_UNPARSEABLE` (stage `forge`, context `{ forge, branch }`).

Testing integration: extend the GitLab discussion fixtures in test/unit/forge/threads-comments.test.ts. Add a GitLab variant of the publish harness in test/unit/workflow/item-threads-index.test.ts using discussions and PUT notes/<id>; enter through postItemThreads, not only a reader helper. Change test/unit/forge/pr.test.ts's malformed-output test from false to rejection, preserving [] as false.

userStories.title: Unresolve re-raised finding threads and preserve visibility on write failure
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add forge unresolve support and reopen resolved own finding threads when the review raises an unsettled finding again.

**Motivation** — When a finding thread was resolved without a settling ruling (the bot judged the earlier finding fixed, or a confirmed finding's fix closed it) and the review raises it again, the edit lands inside the hidden thread.

**Approach** — **C4: unresolve a resolved finding thread when the finding is raised again.** `postPrReview` gains `resolvedThreadIds`, the ids of the bot's own finding threads that are resolved. `writeFinding` edits the own comment as today and then, when its thread is in `resolvedThreadIds`, unresolves the thread. `writeFinding` catches an unresolve failure itself, logs it and returns a flag; `postFindings` then lists the finding off-line in the summary instead of counting it inline, so it stays visible. The existing rethrow of a failed edit of an owned comment is unchanged.

**Scope** — In: unresolveThread and public export, resolved-thread metadata from reviewEnvironment, edit-then-unresolve finding writes, and off-line fallback on failed unresolve. Out: workflow-item reopen notices and publish logic (US-003–US-005), index/summary settlement reporting (US-006–US-007), and ready/push safety (US-008). A bot finding (`f-` key) settled by a writer ruling and raised again by a later review stays settled and skipped; only workflow items are reopened on a re-raise.

**Interface** — New `unresolveThread(ref, thread: Pick<PrThread, "id">, deps, cwd): Promise<void>` in `src/forge/comments.ts`, exported from `@/forge`. GitHub: GraphQL `mutation($id: ID!) { unresolveReviewThread(input: {threadId: $id}) { thread { id isResolved } } }` with the id as a raw `-f id=` variable, as `resolveThread` does. GitLab: `PUT` on the discussion endpoint with `resolved=false`; the discussion id is validated like `resolveThread`'s.

`PostReviewInput` (`src/bot/post.ts`). Target: gains `readonly resolvedThreadIds?: ReadonlySet<string>`.

`reviewEnvironment` (`src/bot/review-run.ts`). Target: sets `resolvedThreadIds` to the ids of `ownFindingThreads` whose `resolved` is `true`.

Failure handling: `unresolveThread` forge write fails — rejects with the `runForgeWrite` error (`FORGE_COMMENT_WRITE_FAILED`). C4 unresolve fails — `warn("bot-post", "Could not reopen a re-raised finding thread", { key, threadId, error })`; the finding goes to the off-line list, not counted inline. Preserve failure propagation for owned edits and skip both writes for settledKeys. Test through postPrReview and through runBotReview, using the existing captured-forge harnesses; keep artifact persistence before forge mutation.

userStories.title: Define reopen notices and invalidate prior item rulings after a notice
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Define the workflow-item reopen wire format and pin how a last-own reopen notice resets ruling state and the reply boundary.

**Motivation** — `postItemThreads` (`src/workflow/item-threads-post.ts`) skips an already-owned item key, and `readThread` takes the last own `wr-` echo as the ruling, so `settleItemThreads` settles a re-raised item from the old ruling.

**Approach** — `readThread` takes the last own comment as the ruling only when it is a `wr-` echo, so after the notice the item has no ruling and stays open until someone rules again.

**Scope** — In: add reopenKey, renderItemReopened and REOPENED_BY_RERAISE to the pure wire-format leaf, and preserve/prove last-own-comment ruling and reply-boundary semantics through readItemThreads and settleItemThreads. Out: forge unresolve (US-002), publish-time selection and writer checks (US-004), closure/retry recovery (US-005), and settled-count/summary rendering (US-006–US-007). Workflow item rulings `waived`, `confirmed` and `overridden` carry over when the same item is raised again; only `fixed` and `verified` are cancelled. This story defines that set but does not implement publish-time selection.

**Interface** — New in `src/workflow/item-threads.ts`: `reopenKey(key) => "wo-" + key`; `renderItemReopened(sha)` => `Raised again by the run at <first 7 of sha>. Reply on this thread to rule on it.`; `REOPENED_BY_RERAISE: ReadonlySet<Disposition>` = `fixed`, `verified`.

Use the existing SHORT_SHA_CHARS convention and keep these helpers separate from I/O. The existing readThread algorithm already bases ruling parsing on the last own marked comment and filters replies after that boundary; do not replace it with a scan that recovers a superseded wr- echo. Tests belong with the existing wire-format and item-thread-state fixtures. Preserve the existing malformed-opener guard: a later reopen marker cannot manufacture a readable item when parseItemOpener rejects its opener.

[unit] renderItemReopened("a".repeat(40)) returns "Raised again by the run at aaaaaaa. Reply on this thread to rule on it.".
[unit] REOPENED_BY_RERAISE has exactly two members, fixed and verified.
[unit] When readItemThreads reads an item thread made of the opener, a wr-fixed-<key> echo, and then an own comment marked reopenKey(<key>), it returns that item with no ruling.
[unit] In that case the item's replies contain only the comments after the reopen notice.
[unit] settleItemThreads puts that item in open.
[unit] When a thread's opener cannot be parsed by parseItemOpener, readItemThreads returns no item for that thread, even if a later own comment carries reopenKey(<key>).

routing.reasoning: Only item-threads.ts needs additive production helpers; the existing last-own-comment reader already resets rulings after a notice, so focused wire/state TDD suffices without new I/O or permission decisions.

userStories.title: Reopen re-raised fixed and verified workflow items after a newly reviewed head
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Reopen still-raised fixed/verified workflow items when publish records a different fully reviewed head, without hiding a writer's pending reply.

**Motivation** — `postItemThreads` (`src/workflow/item-threads-post.ts`) skips an already-owned item key, and `readThread` takes the last own `wr-` echo as the ruling, so `settleItemThreads` settles a re-raised item from the old ruling.

**Approach** — **C2: a re-raise by a newly reviewed head reopens fixed/verified items.** At publish, `postItemThreads` already computes the index's reviewed head through `reviewedIndex(input, read.index)`. When that returns a `reviewedHead` that differs from the previous index's `reviewedHead`, the run reviewed new code; a previous index with no reviewed head (`Reviewed head: none`, written by an incomplete review) counts as different, so the first fully reviewed run after it can reopen. For each owned item thread whose key is among this publish's item keys, whose current ruling is `fixed` or `verified`, and which has no reply from a writer after that ruling (a writer's pending reply already keeps the item open and must not be hidden behind the notice; a reply from someone without write access is dropped by `settleItemThreads`, so it must not block the reopen), nax replies on the thread with a reopen notice (marker key `reopenKey(key)` = `wo-<key>`) and unresolves the thread. `readThread` takes the last own comment as the ruling only when it is a `wr-` echo, so after the notice the item has no ruling and stays open until someone rules again. A publish whose reviewed head did not change (a CI-repair republish, a resume, an incomplete review) never reopens a ruled item.

The writer check reuses `writerCheck` and `hasWriteAccess` from `@/forge`, with the same cache and fail-closed rule the recorder uses: a login whose check rejects counts as having no write access, so the reopen goes ahead.

**Scope** — In: ruled-item selection, exported reviewedIndex, cached fail-closed writer checks, notice then unresolve, warning/failure aggregation, and publish seam integration. Out: closed-item selection, unresolve-only retry and keepReviewed recovery (US-005), settled-count presentation (US-006), finding reopening implementation (US-002), and summary changes (US-007). Workflow item rulings `waived`, `confirmed` and `overridden` carry over when the same item is raised again; only `fixed` and `verified` are cancelled. A publish whose reviewed head is unset or unchanged (CI-repair republish, resume, incomplete review) never reopens a ruled item, even when the ruling predates the run.

**Interface** — `reviewedIndex(input, previous)` (`src/workflow/item-threads-index.ts`). Baseline: module-private. Target: exported, behaviour unchanged. Existing signature: `reviewedIndex(input: ItemThreadsInput, previous: ItemIndex | undefined): Omit<ItemIndex, "keys">`.

New `src/workflow/item-threads-reopen.ts`: `reopenReraisedItems(input: ItemThreadsInput, keys: readonly string[], context: ReopenContext): Promise<{ reopened: ReadonlySet<string>; failed: number }>`, with `ReopenContext = { ref, read, login, deps, cwd, info }` (the fields `maintainItemIndex`'s context already has). This story covers the ruled-item case only, including the writer-reply check. `reopened` holds every key a reopen was attempted for, whether or not the write succeeded; those keys never count as settled. The notice's sha is `input.head`, falling back to `info.headSha`.

`postItemThreads`. Target: after posting new items, calls `reopenReraisedItems`, adds its `failed` to the outcome, then calls `maintainItemIndex`. `ItemThreadsOutcome` is unchanged. The keepReviewed and settled options are added by US-005 and US-006 respectively.

Failure handling: C2 reopen reply fails — `warn("item-threads", "[item-threads] Reopen write failed", { itemId, error })`; no unresolve; outcome `failed` + 1. C2 unresolve fails after the reply — same warning; outcome `failed` + 1. US-005 adds provenance retention and retry behavior for both failures. Writer check for a reply rejects — that reply's author counts as having no write access; the reopen goes ahead.

Use US-002's unresolveThread and US-003's reopenKey, renderItemReopened and REOPENED_BY_RERAISE. Create test/unit/workflow/item-threads-reopen.test.ts with a captured-forge publish harness modeled on item-threads-index.test.ts; all seam assertions enter postItemThreads, including writer/nonwriter permissions, review provenance, ordering and failed writes.

userStories.title: Reopen re-raised closed items and retry incomplete reopen writes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Reopen currently closed items on any publish and make partial reopen writes retryable without duplicating notices or advancing reviewed provenance.

**Motivation** — `postItemThreads` (`src/workflow/item-threads-post.ts`) skips an already-owned item key, and `readThread` takes the last own `wr-` echo as the ruling, so `settleItemThreads` settles a re-raised item from the old ruling.

**Approach** — A **closed item raised again** is reopened the same way, at any publish: an owned item thread whose last own comment is its closure notice (`closedKey(key)`, written when the item dropped out of a run) and whose key is among this publish's keys gets the reopen notice and is unresolved. Without this the item is open for readiness but its thread stays resolved and reads "No longer open".

A reopen write that fails is retried at the next publish. When `reopenReraisedItems` reports `failed > 0`, the index keeps the previous index's reviewed head and base instead of the new ones, so the next fully reviewed publish still sees a changed head and retries a failed reply. A notice that was posted but whose unresolve failed leaves the thread with the notice as its last own comment and still resolved; at any publish where its key is among the keys, `reopenReraisedItems` unresolves such a thread again without posting a second notice. Readiness is unaffected; only the next review's incremental range starts earlier.

The writer check reuses `writerCheck` and `hasWriteAccess` from `@/forge`, with the same cache and fail-closed rule the recorder uses: a login whose check rejects counts as having no write access, so the reopen goes ahead.

**Scope** — In: extend US-004's helper with closed-item and unresolve-only cases; preserve previous reviewed head/base after any failed reopen; keep failure aggregation and attempt sets. Out: new settled-count rendering and recorder refresh (US-006), summary/body changes (US-007), and finding mutation behavior (US-002). A reopened item that later drops out of a run again is not re-closed: `maintainItemIndex` skips any thread that already has an own closure notice, so the thread stays open with its reopen notice. Readiness is unaffected.

**Interface** — `reopenReraisedItems(input: ItemThreadsInput, keys: readonly string[], context: ReopenContext): Promise<{ reopened: ReadonlySet<string>; failed: number }>`, with `ReopenContext = { ref, read, login, deps, cwd, info }`. It handles a closed item (last own comment `closedKey(key)`) at any publish, and an already-posted notice whose thread is still resolved, unresolved without a second notice. `reopened` holds every key a reopen was attempted for, whether or not the write succeeded; those keys never count as settled. The notice's sha is `input.head`, falling back to `info.headSha`.

`maintainItemIndex(input, keys, context)`. Target after US-005: `maintainItemIndex(input, keys, context, options: { keepReviewed?: boolean } = {})`, where `reviewed` is the previous index's `reviewedHead`/`reviewedBase` when `keepReviewed` is true, else `reviewedIndex(input, read.index)`.

`postItemThreads`. Target: after posting new items, calls `reopenReraisedItems`, adds its `failed` to the outcome, then calls `maintainItemIndex` with the previous index's reviewed head and base kept when that `failed` is above 0. `ItemThreadsOutcome` is unchanged.

Failure handling: C2 reopen reply fails — `warn("item-threads", "[item-threads] Reopen write failed", { itemId, error })`; no unresolve; outcome `failed` + 1; the index keeps the previous reviewed head, so the next fully reviewed publish retries. C2 unresolve fails after the reply — same warning; outcome `failed` + 1; the index keeps the previous reviewed head; the item is open (its last own comment is the notice), and a later publish unresolves the thread without a second notice. Extend the US-004 test harness and enter all integration seams through postItemThreads.

userStories.title: Show settled item counts in the durable index at publish and after rulings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Display settled workflow-item counts in the index while keeping readiness state and index provenance unchanged.

**Motivation** — `maintainItemIndex` is called only at publish; `renderReviewSummary` counts `threadsAnswered` only.

**Approach** — **#2694: show settlement.** The index's first line becomes `nax workflow items: <N> (<S> settled)`. The listed keys, their count and the reviewed head/base lines are unchanged, so readiness is unchanged; `S` is presentation only and `parseItemIndex` does not return it. The parser still accepts the legacy `nax workflow open items: <N>` line. The publish writes `S` as the number of this publish's keys whose thread carries a ruling with no later reply and was not just reopened. `recordPrRulings` rewrites the index comment after settlement when its `S` changes.

**Scope** — In: backward-compatible parser/new writer, publish settled-count computation excluding all reopen attempts, maintainItemIndex settled option, and best-effort recorder index refresh. Out: summary ItemStatus and draft instructions (US-007), reopen selection/recovery algorithms (US-004–US-005), and ready/push changes (US-008). The publish's settled count does not run the writer permission check; a thread with any reply after its ruling counts as not settled. The index rewrite in `recordPrRulings` edits from the comment snapshot it read; it does not re-read the index first, so a publish that rewrote the index in between can be overwritten until the next publish. An older nax install that reads the new index line treats the PR as having no item index and holds readiness until upgraded.

**Interface** — `renderItemIndex(index)`. Target: `renderItemIndex(index: ItemIndex, settled = 0): string`, first line `nax workflow items: <keys.length> (<settled> settled)`.

`parseItemIndex(body)`. Target: accepts either first line `nax workflow open items: <N>` or `nax workflow items: <N> (<S> settled)`; returns `null` when `S > N`; returns the same `ItemIndex` shape as today (no settled field).

`maintainItemIndex(input, keys, context)`. userStories.title: Bind bot-fix ready and push writes to the intended PR and head
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Mark the intended PR ready only after validating its expected head, keep reporting after rejected ready writes, and protect pushes with an explicit lease.

**Motivation** — On the non-workflow path `readyStep` marks ready right after `waitForCi`, with no head re-read.

**Approach** — **C3/C5/C7: ready and push.** `readyStep` marks ready with `markReadyArgv(env.ref.forge, env.info.url)` on both paths. On the non-workflow path, after the green CI wait and after the existing `throwIfAborted()`, it re-reads the PR and holds when the head is not the expected sha, `state.pushedSha ?? env.info.headSha` (the value `waitForCi` already binds CI to). A non-zero ready exit becomes a hold (`readyHeld: "could not mark ready: …"`) so `reportStep` still runs. `pushStep` adds `--force-with-lease=refs/heads/<headRef>:<info.headSha>`.

**Scope** — In: bot-fix ready URL targeting on both paths, non-workflow post-green head reread, report-bound ready-write holds, and real push lease for temporary/in-place checkouts. Out: malformed hasOpenPr output (US-001), forge unresolve writes (US-002), workflow reraising/index/summary changes (US-003–US-007), and existing C6 gates/conflict control flow. US-008 only: a ready write rejected for reasons other than a non-zero exit (spawn failure, abort) still rejects as today. The `--dry-run` push access probe keeps its argv; only the real push gains the lease. `bindToHead` keeps letting a green poll with no sha through; the non-workflow ready path closes the gap with its own head re-read instead.

**Interface** — `readyStep(env, state)`. Existing signature: `readyStep(env: BotFixEnv, state: BotFixState): Promise<StepResult<BotFixState>>`. Keep `waitForPrHead`, `waitForCi`, `workflowReadyHold` and `_fixReportDeps.readPrInfo` as the existing seams. Both paths use `markReadyArgv(env.ref.forge, env.info.url)`.

`pushStep(env, state)`. Baseline argv `["push", "--no-verify", "origin", "HEAD:refs/heads/<headRef>"]`. Target: `["push", "--no-verify", "--force-with-lease=refs/heads/<headRef>:<env.info.headSha>", "origin", "HEAD:refs/heads/<headRef>"]`.

Failure handling: PR re-read after green CI rejects (non-workflow ready path) — `readyHeld: "PR head could not be re-read"`, not marked ready. PR re-read shows another head — `readyHeld: "PR head changed since this execution"`, not marked ready. Ready command exits non-zero — `readyHeld: "could not mark ready: <trimmed stderr>"`, or `"could not mark ready: exit code <n>"` when stderr is empty; exit `report`. Push rejected by the lease — existing `push-rejected` outcome. Update test/integration/bot/fix-report-workflow.test.ts's ready target to s.env.info.url, preserving its evidence/order assertion. Goal and completion: close #2694 by making GitLab comment classification, workflow item reraising, finding-thread visibility, settlement presentation, and bot-fix remote writes reflect durable PR state across reruns. This is an enhancement of existing TypeScript/Bun code, entirely inside packages/nax; no new service, dependency, configuration, package release, or storage migration is required. Preserve exactly US-001 through US-008 and their specified dependencies. Implement the independent forge, wire-format, summary, and fix-path stories alongside the sequential reopen chain US-002/US-003 -> US-004 -> US-005 -> US-006. Navigation: codebase-memory MCP was unavailable in this session; findings below come from direct source reads and text searches rooted at the supplied execution repository. The marker grammar currently lives at packages/nax/src/forge/marker.ts:14, and marker.ts already imports threads at line 3: importing marker.ts back from threads.ts would create a runtime cycle. Create the leaf marker-grammar.ts, move the grammar without changing validation, last-valid-marker parsing, wrapper, or stripping semantics, and retain marker.ts re-exports. Public consumers use packages/nax/src/forge/index.ts:35; add TOP_LEVEL_MARKER_KEYS there. Ownership remains author===login plus valid marker (packages/nax/src/forge/marker.ts:42), never marker alone. This reader fix automatically restores postSummary's top-level own-summary lookup (packages/nax/src/bot/post.ts:277), readItemThreads' top-level index lookup (packages/nax/src/workflow/item-thread-state.ts:48), and evidence lookups in packages/nax/src/bot/fix-report.ts:198. outOfScope: A bot finding (`f-` key) settled by a writer ruling and raised again by a later review stays settled and skipped; only workflow items are reopened on a re-raise.
Workflow item rulings `waived`, `confirmed` and `overridden` carry over when the same item is raised again; only `fixed` and `verified` are cancelled.
A publish whose reviewed head is unset or unchanged (CI-repair republish, resume, incomplete review) never reopens a ruled item, even when the ruling predates the run.

A reopened item that later drops out of a run again is not re-closed: `maintainItemIndex` skips any thread that already has an own closure notice, so the thread stays open with its reopen notice. Readiness is unaffected.

The index rewrite in `recordPrRulings` edits from the comment snapshot it read; it does not re-read the index first, so a publish that rewrote the index in between can be overwritten until the next publish.
US-008 only: a ready write rejected for reasons other than a non-zero exit (spawn failure, abort) still rejects as today.
The review summary does not link each recorded item to its thread; it names id, disposition and who ruled.
The `nax bot fix` "Nothing to fix" comment does not list recorded rulings.
Finding rulings echoed by `recordFindingRulings` are not listed in the new item-rulings summary line; they stay in the existing counts.
The publish's settled count does not run the writer permission check; a thread with any reply after its ruling counts as not settled.
An older nax install that reads the new index line treats the PR as having no item index and holds readiness until upgraded.
A GitLab discussion opened by someone else with a forged top-level marker is flattened into top-level comments; it gains no ownership and stays behind the writer gate.
The `--dry-run` push access probe keeps its argv; only the real push gains the lease.
`bindToHead` keeps letting a green poll with no sha through; the non-workflow ready path closes the gap with its own head re-read instead.
